授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: In this course, students learn the fundamentals of physics, including description of motion, the three laws of motion, work and energy, momentum and collisions, and rotation and oscillation, using knowledge of vectors, derivatives, and integrals. The goal is also to apply the knowledge learned and to develop insight into the physics behind natural phenomena through logical thinking and data analysis.
advice:
Logical thinking and data analysis are conducted based on actual measurement data, and the ability to gain insight into the physics behind natural phenomena is nurtured. We will cover the following topics:

1. Dimension and units.
2. Motion in one dimension.
3. Motion in two dimensions.
4. Newton's laws of motion.
5. Energy of a system.
6. Conservation of energy.
7. Rotational motion.
8. Oscillatory motion.

Students are required to have a knowledge of vectors, differentiation, and integration.
Students will learn a number of formulas related to the laws of physics. Students will not only be expected to memorize the formulas but also be required to understand the meaning of these formulas.

activityGoals.body: Basic knowledge of mechanics such as speed, acceleration, and force.
Ability to evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton’s equations of motion.
Ability to calculate potential energy using integral calculus and a knowledge of work and energy.
Ability to understand mechanical energy, conservation of momentum, and conservation of angular momentum.
Ability to perform data analysis using measured data and interpret the data based on logical thinking.
Ability to understand the content of the lesson by completing the homework and paticipating in group activities.

Accurately evaluate the motion of an object by deriving and solving Newton's equations of motion.
Accurately calculate potential energy using integral calculus based on a knowledge of work and energy.
Accurately identify conserved quantities in physical phenomena by using the laws of conservation of mechanical energy, momentum, and angular momentum.
Analyze data using measured data to interpret data based on logical thinking.

              In this course, students learn the fundamentals of physics, including description of motion, the three laws of motion, work and energy, momentum and collisions, and rotation and oscillation, using knowledge of vectors, derivatives, and integrals. The goal is also to apply the knowledge learned and to develop insight into the physics behind natural phenomena through logical thinking and data analysis.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Logical thinking and data analysis are conducted based on actual measurement data, and the ability to gain insight into the physics behind natural phenomena is nurtured. We will cover the following topics:

1. Dimension and units.
2. Motion in one dimension.
3. Motion in two dimensions.
4. Newton's laws of motion.
5. Energy of a system.
6. Conservation of energy.
7. Rotational motion.
8. Oscillatory motion.

Students are required to have a knowledge of vectors, differentiation, and integration.
Students will learn a number of formulas related to the laws of physics. Students will not only be expected to memorize the formulas but also be required to understand the meaning of these formulas.
